text.p: Mercury Finance Co said Tuesday it has chosen Arthur Andersen Llp as its new auditor, replacing KPMG Peat Marwick.
Mercury said last month it had to restate earnings lower by about $90 million over the past four years, due to accounting irregularities.
The company blamed the accounting misstatements on its controller, James Doyle, who has been relieved of his duties.

But Doyle's attorney accused the company of engaging in a charade and said Doyle was cooperating with federal authorities. FBI agents have served a search warrant on the company, seeking financial records, the company said.

Mercury has defaulted on millions of dollars in debt and lost more than $2 billion in market capitalization, but said last week it secured $50 million in financing to meet operating expenses in the near term.

The company also appointed turnaround and bankruptcy specialist William Brandt Jr as president and chief executive officer. Brandt Tuesday said the sub-prime auto lender has asked Arthur Andersen to proceed as expeditiously as possible with the 1996 audit.
"Under the circumstances, Mercury Finance will be best served by a new public accounting firm, which can bring a fresh and independent point of view to the situation," Brandt said in a news release.
Mercury shares were down 1/8 at 2-1/8 Tuesday.
